issues.claim: "Во встроенном контейнере .NET 10 нет API для декораторов" / "The built-in container in .NET 10 has no decorator API" and option d: "no Decorate method on IServiceCollection"
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt of the dependency-injection overview page (and the TryAddScoped page) never states that the built-in container lacks decorator support, so the cited link does not show support for the central claim. From my own knowledge M.E.DI has no Decorate in .NET 10, but the generator itself flagged this as unverified. The same applies to "Since .NET 8" for AddKeyedScoped/GetRequiredKeyedService, which no cited excerpt confirms.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a source that supports the claims (for example the Microsoft Learn keyed-services section of the DI docs, and the dotnet/runtime issue requesting decorator support that is still open), or move the claim out of a linked-source role. Re-open the pages and confirm the wording before setting the verified date.

issues.problem: TryAddScoped lives in the Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Extensions namespace and needs an extra using. Option c is still correct in behaviour, because the call is ignored when the service type is already registered, but a reader could think it does not compile.
issues.suggestedFix: Mention `using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Extensions;` in the prompt or option explanation, or leave as is since the behaviour is correct.

issues.claim: "Во время выполнения ничего не проверяется." / "Nothing is checked at run time."
issues.problem: This is true of the language and compiler, but System.Text.Json (.NET 7+) does enforce the presence of required members at run time during deserialization. It does not enforce non-null, so option c is still false. The blanket statement is slightly overbroad.
issues.suggestedFix: Write: "The language itself checks nothing at run time (some libraries, such as System.Text.Json, check that a required member is present during deserialization, but not that it is non-null)." Apply the same change to the en text.

issues.claim: "an `init` accessor allows assignment only during initialization: in an initializer, in `with`, in a constructor"
issues.problem: The fetched init page excerpt does not show `with` or the constructor list explicitly. The claim is correct per the C# spec for init accessors (initializer, `with`, constructors of the type or a derived type, other init accessors).
issues.suggestedFix: Optionally add the C# 9 init-only setters spec or the records `with` expression page as a link. No change to the text is needed.
